summary: InterlockedPushEntrySList, InterlockedPopEntrySList and InterlockedFlushSList on headers InitializeSListHead made: the header's first entry, depth and sequence after each call, the values returned, the entries' links, the last error left, and two threads pushing onto one list at once.
applicability: windows-2022 (AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor); windows-2025 (AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor)

acceptance.derivation: scripts/family_run.py slist_rows: Interlocked lists (Sprint 063): a push advances the header's sequence by 2 on Server 2025 and by 1 on 2022 (row push.1); pop and flush leave it. The sequence is kept as the count of pushes it stands for, the step being push.1's.

evidence.quote: The return value is the previous first item in the list. If the list was previously empty, the return value is NULL. ... All list items must be aligned on a MEMORY_ALLOCATION_ALIGNMENT boundary; otherwise, this function will behave unpredictably.

open_questions: The sequence advances by 2 a push on Server 2025 and by 1 on 2022; the rows keep the count of pushes, and w2m advances it as Server 2025 does, the game's reference system (game run 38206263976).
A header or entry off a 16-byte boundary has no row: Microsoft Learn says the functions behave unpredictably, and w2m stops the run.
